raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

#44643 caches the fused linear-GELU verdict per linear in a module-level `WeakKeyDictionary`, `_VERDICTS`. Under `torch.compile`, dynamo guards on that dict's size. DiT blocks share one compiled forward, so every new linear a block brings changes the size and recompiles the frame. On 4xB300, an LTX-2 compile run logged this on both ranks:

```
torch._dynamo hit config.recompile_limit (64) ... ltx_2.py:1263 ... last reason: len(...fused_linear_gelu_site._VERDICTS.data) != 28
```

After that, the blocks ran eager behind failing guards on every call.

This fixes a regression introduced by #44643 (same author).

## Modifications

In `fused_linear_gelu_site.py`, `can_use_linear_gelu` computes the input-independent verdict directly while tracing (`torch.compiler.is_compiling()`), as it did before #44643. Eager calls keep the cache. The verdict is the same either way, so outputs are unchanged.

New CUDA test `test_mounted_gelu_sites_compile_one_frame_across_linears` in `test_sites.py`: 12 blocks with two mounted sites each must compile to one frame. On H200 it fails on main and passes here (`test_sites.py` 27/27; with the dynamic-LoRA PR merged in, `test_sites.py` + `test_quality_fusion_lora.py` 32/32).

This PR and "[Fix] diffusion: Keep dynamic LoRA deltas on fused linear-GELU sites" both edit `can_use_linear_gelu`. They merge cleanly in either order. The LoRA PR's adapter check sits above this PR's compile branch, so it also applies while tracing; keep that order if either one is rebased.

## Accuracy Tests

The same verdict is computed, so the same path runs and outputs are unchanged.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

LTX-2 two-stage, compile profile, 2xH200, two interleaved rounds (e2e):

| | round 1 | round 2 |
|---|---|---|
| main | 10.754 s | 10.487 s |
| this PR | 10.152 s | 9.915 s |

That is −5.5% in both rounds:
- stage-1 step time: 0.198–0.206 s → 0.185–0.190 s;
- server ready: 128 s → 104 s;
- the `recompile_limit` line is gone from the log.

LTX-2 under compile is still slower than eager on H200, because of graph breaks after attention. That is out of scope here.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

@@ -138,6 +138,9 @@ def can_use_linear_gelu(linear: Any, x: torch.Tensor) -> bool:
         return False
     if getattr(linear, "weight", None) is None or x.dtype != linear.weight.dtype:
         return False
+    if torch.compiler.is_compiling():
+        # dynamo guards on the cache's size, so reading it recompiles per linear
+        return _input_independent_ok(linear)
     verdict = _VERDICTS.get(linear)
     if verdict is None:
         verdict = _VERDICTS[linear] = _input_independent_ok(linear)

@@ -22,6 +22,7 @@
 
 import pytest
 import torch
+import torch._dynamo.testing
 import torch.nn as nn
 import torch.nn.functional as F
 
@@ -503,6 +504,33 @@ def test_mounted_gelu_site_compiles_fullgraph():
     )
 
 
+class _GeluBlock(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.ff = _GeluSite()
+        self.audio_ff = _GeluSite()
+
+    def forward(self, x):
+        return self.ff(x) + self.audio_ff(x)
+
+
+@requires_cuda
+@torch.no_grad()
+def test_mounted_gelu_sites_compile_one_frame_across_linears():
+    # DiT blocks share one compiled forward; a new linear must not recompile it
+    torch._dynamo.reset()
+    blocks = nn.ModuleList(_GeluBlock() for _ in range(12))
+    assert linear_gelu.FUSED_LINEAR_GELU.mount(blocks)
+    counter = torch._dynamo.testing.CompileCounter()
+    for block in blocks:
+        block.compile(backend=counter)
+    x = torch.randn(16, 64, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    for _ in range(2):
+        for block in blocks:
+            block(x)
+    assert counter.frame_count == 1
+
